**4B.4 Research Note**
**Working verdict:** **mixed, leaning no**. Marcos showed some deference to formal institutions in 2024, but I found little evidence that he materially strengthened independent courts, legislatures, audit bodies, or local governments when they could constrain him. The record is stronger on executive-managed reform and selective institutional deference than on durable empowerment of oversight bodies.

| Direction | Claim-level item | Source | Date | URL | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Marcos told critics to let Comelec handle allegations that signatures in the people’s initiative drive may have been bought. That is a modest sign of deference to the election commission rather than direct executive interference. | GMA News Online | 2024-01-23 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/895067/marcos-on-people-s-initiative-for-cha-cha-let-comelec-do-their-job/story/ | 4B.4, 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Positive / mixed | The Supreme Court rejected red-tagging as a threat to life, liberty, and security. In the material I found, Marcos did not retaliate against that judicial constraint, which slightly favors respect for an independent court. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-08 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/08/philippines-supreme-court-rejects-red-tagging | 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2 |
| Positive / mixed | The DOJ created a task force to investigate Duterte-era extrajudicial killings and file charges if warranted. That is a real accountability move, though it remains inside the executive rather than a fully independent oversight gain. | Philippine News Agency | 2024-11-06 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1237266 | 4B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Positive / mixed | Marcos pushed procurement reform to shorten timelines, standardize forms, and institutionalize e-procurement. That cuts against pure patronage governance and can support oversight, though it is not a direct empowerment of an independent watchdog. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/ | 4B.4, 4B.2 |
| Positive / mixed | The administration expanded eFOI access and kept a media-literacy / disinformation campaign in place. That modestly supports institutional transparency and external scrutiny. | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-18 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036 | 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2 |
| Mixed | Marcos reorganized the National Security Council into a more resilient institution with cabinet, legislative, military, intelligence, and legal members. This is institutional governance, but it also centralizes presidential discretion rather than clearly strengthening an independent check. | Lawphil / Office of the President | 2024-12-30 | https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_81_2024.html | 4B.4, 3B.9, 4B.2 |
| Negative | HRW said red-tagging under Marcos placed leftist activists and critics at serious risk, with officials and supporters accusing them of communist ties. That is inconsistent with a ruler who is genuinely strengthening independent oversight and constraint. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8 |
| Negative | HRW reported Marcos-era officials and police or military members repeatedly visited union leaders and threatened them by linking them to communism. This is direct intimidation of civil-society monitoring and independent organization. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8 |
| Negative | Freedom House says elections are free from overt restrictions, but not fully fair because disinformation and vote buying distort competition; it also says red-tagging persisted under Marcos. That is a broad warning that independent institutions were not enough to cleanly constrain the executive environment. | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024 | 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Negative | The Reuters Institute says red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted under Marcos. That indicates weak protection for outside scrutiny even where formal institutions existed. | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2 |
| Negative | The U.S. State Department report says credible killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, media restrictions, and threats to labor activists remained. This is not consistent with robustly empowered oversight institutions. | U.S. State Department via ecoi.net | 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html | 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.1 |

**Bottom line:** there is some evidence of institutional respect and limited accountability moves, but not strong evidence that Marcos systematically strengthened independent courts, legislatures, audit bodies, or local governments when they constrained him.

**Search gap:** I did not find strong 2024 evidence of Marcos materially empowering the legislature, COA-style audit bodies, or local government autonomy against his own preferences. The record is much clearer on selective deference to Comelec and the Supreme Court, and much weaker on durable expansion of independent oversight.
